name: Neem
desc: A tree widely used in traditional Indian medicine for skin and cleansing routines.
traditional: Traditionally used for skin comfort, oral care, and general cleansing practices.
research: Laboratory studies show antimicrobial activity; small clinical studies exist for skin uses with mixed results.
forms: tablets, powders, oils, soaps, face wash
safety: Generally used traditionally; skin patch-testing advised for topicals.
interactions: May interact with diabetes and immune medicines; check with a clinician.
children: Topical use common; supervise young children.

name: Aloe Vera
desc: A succulent plant whose gel is traditionally applied to skin.
traditional: Traditionally used for skin soothing, minor burns comfort, and digestive routines.
research: Some evidence for skin hydration and minor-burn comfort; digestive evidence limited.
safety: Topical use generally mild; latex part (aloin) can irritate and act as laxative.
interactions: Oral latex may interact with medicines affecting minerals and blood sugar.
pregnancy: Avoid oral latex; topical use discuss with clinician.

name: Turmeric
desc: A golden spice central to cooking and traditional medicine.
traditional: Traditionally used for joint comfort, digestion, and skin routines.
research: Curcumin has been studied in many small trials; absorption is poor and results mixed.
safety: Culinary use safe; high-dose supplements need clinician input.
interactions: May interact with blood thinners and diabetes medicines.
pregnancy: Culinary amounts fine; supplements need advice.

name: Tulsi (Holy Basil)
desc: A revered adaptogenic herb widely consumed as tea.
traditional: Traditionally used for respiratory comfort, stress routines, and daily wellness teas.
research: Small trials suggest stress and metabolic markers may shift; evidence preliminary.
safety: Tea use generally mild; discuss concentrated extracts with a clinician.
interactions: May interact with blood-sugar and blood-pressure medicines.
pregnancy: Tea in moderation generally used; extracts need advice.

name: Ginger
desc: A warming rhizome used worldwide in food and traditional medicine.
traditional: Traditionally used for digestive comfort, nausea routines, and cold-season teas.
research: Reasonable evidence for nausea relief; other uses mixed.
safety: Culinary use safe; large doses may cause heartburn.
interactions: High doses may interact with blood thinners.
pregnancy: Small culinary amounts generally used; supplements need advice.

name: Honey
desc: A natural sweetener traditionally used for throat soothing.
traditional: Traditionally used for cough and throat comfort in warm fluids.
research: Some evidence for nighttime cough soothing in children over one year.
safety: NEVER for infants under 12 months (botulism risk).
interactions: Minimal; sugar content matters in diabetes.

name: Triphala
desc: A classic three-fruit Ayurvedic preparation for digestive regularity.
traditional: Classically used for bowel regularity and digestive balance.
research: Small studies on bowel function with mixed results.
safety: Follow label doses; prolonged use needs review.
contra: Bowel obstruction symptoms; pregnancy without advice.

name: Giloy (Guduchi)
desc: A climbing shrub central to Ayurvedic fever-care traditions.
traditional: Traditionally used in fever care and general wellness routines.
research: Early small studies; liver-safety signals reported in rare cases — medical supervision advised.
safety: Rare liver-injury reports exist; use only with clinician awareness.
interactions: May interact with immune and diabetes medicines.

name: Amla
desc: A vitamin-C-rich fruit used in food and traditional preparations.
traditional: Traditionally used for digestion, hair routines, and general vitality.
safety: Food use safe; concentrated doses need input.
interactions: High doses may affect blood sugar medicines.

name: Bhumi Amla
desc: A small herb traditionally associated with liver and urinary comfort.
traditional: Classically referenced for liver and urinary routines.
research: Early laboratory and small clinical work; not established treatment.
safety: Use under qualified guidance, especially with liver conditions.

name: Peppermint
desc: A cooling aromatic herb used for head and digestive comfort.
traditional: Traditionally used for head comfort routines and digestion.
research: Peppermint oil has small studies for tension-type headache; evidence limited.
safety: Essential oil must be diluted; keep from young children's faces.
contra: Undiluted oil on skin; infants for strong preparations.
pregnancy: Mild tea use common; oil needs advice.

name: Boswellia (Shallaki)
desc: A resin traditionally used for joint comfort.
traditional: Classically referenced for joint and mobility routines.
research: Small trials for joint comfort with mixed results.
safety: Generally tolerated; clinician input for long use.

name: Bakuchi
desc: A seed traditionally referenced for pigment-related routines.
traditional: Classically referenced for skin pigment routines under strict supervision.
research: Early studies exist; photosensitivity risk is significant.
safety: Causes sun sensitivity; NEVER casual use.
contra: Unsupervised use; fair sun-sensitive skin caution.

name: Gokshura
desc: A herb traditionally associated with urinary comfort.
research: Limited modern evidence for urinary outcomes.
safety: Use under guidance with kidney conditions.

name: Ashwagandha
desc: An adaptogenic root widely used for stress and sleep routines.
traditional: Traditionally used for stress routines, sleep support, and vitality.
research: Small trials suggest stress/sleep marker shifts; rare liver signals reported.
safety: Use with clinician awareness; rare liver-injury reports.
interactions: May add to sedatives; thyroid and immune medicines.
